checks.TARGET_COMMITMENT: That the review does not rank the two artists and does not gather them into a group.
checks.SENTENCE_NOW: Two of the artists the review takes up can be set down beside each other because of what it happens to record about each.
checks.WHAT_IT_NOW_COMMITS_TO: That the review takes up at least two artists and records something about each of them, and that the writer is choosing to place those two side by side on the basis of that recorded material. It makes no claim about what the review declines to do.
checks.REASON: The negative claim about the review's own behaviour (no ranking, no grouping) is gone in every form; a reader is no longer told what the review does not do. The pairing is now presented as the writer's own comparative move, which is legitimate interpretation, and the only source-meta content left ('what it happens to record about each') is that the review records material on each artist, which the source text plainly does. 'happens to' colours the recording as incidental but does not tell the reader the review withholds ranking or grouping, so it is not a weaker form of the target. No substitute fact, name or number was invented and the sentence reads coherently.

checks.TARGET_COMMITMENT: That the venue holding the Sandra George show is named City Art Centre.
checks.SENTENCE_NOW: Whatever the visitor is doing in the gallery at City Art Gallery or at Ingleby, it is happening now, and it is happening to a person who did not know the work existed.
checks.WHAT_IT_NOW_COMMITS_TO: That there are shows at a venue called City Art Gallery and at Ingleby, that a visitor's activity there is present-tense, and that this visitor previously did not know the work existed.
checks.REASON: The venue name asserted is now 'City Art Gallery', which is exactly what the source gives ('her show at City Art Gallery'); the 'City Art Centre' naming is gone in every form, including as presupposition, and no shortened or paraphrased version of it survives. 'Ingleby' is also source-licensed (the group show centred on Frank Walter). No source-supported material was stripped by this renaming and no new fact, number or name was introduced by it. The claim about the visitor's prior ignorance is pre-existing content targeted by a separate patch, not damage created by this proper-noun repair; 'the gallery at City Art Gallery' is redundant phrasing but grammatical.

checks.TARGET_COMMITMENT: That the visitor's state of not knowing the work existed held as of one hour earlier.
checks.SENTENCE_NOW: Whatever the visitor is doing in the gallery at City Art Gallery or at Ingleby, it is happening now, and it is happening to a person who did not know the work existed.
checks.WHAT_IT_NOW_COMMITS_TO: That the visitor's activity is happening in the present, and that this same visitor was, at some point before now, in a state of not knowing that the work existed.
checks.REASON: The one-hour measure is gone, but the target commitment is a temporally indexed mental state, and the sentence still asserts the state itself: 'a person who did not know the work existed', set against 'it is happening now', still tells the reader that this visitor's ignorance held at an earlier point and ended at the visit. That is a shorter, weaker form of the same claim rather than its removal, and the rubric counts shorter and weaker forms as non-closure. The source establishes only that George, Walter and Hasegawa never showed work publicly in their lifetimes and were undiscovered; it says nothing about what any visitor knew or did not know, so the surviving human-state assertion is still unsupported. No hedge was added, no substitute fact appeared, and the sentence is grammatical.
